$comment: Every moon's surface (#37, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Moon surfaces"). `sources` are the image sources with their credit and licence (src/data/credits.json is built from them for the help page). `maps` are real spacecraft maps, processed by `pnpm gen:surfaces` (download, align the prime meridian to the map centre, colour a grey mosaic along `hue`/`darkHue`, fill a partial map, set the brightness from `albedo`). `painted` and `families` are painted surfaces for moons no spacecraft has mapped: the recipe gives colour, brightness and the kind of pattern, `basis` says what that rests on. Every moon of the data must appear exactly once.

orbitalia-painted.title: Painted surfaces
orbitalia-painted.credit: Orbitalia contributors (scripts/lib/paint.ts), from published colours and brightness (albedo) measurements
orbitalia-painted.note: Not a photograph: no spacecraft has mapped these moons, so their colour, brightness and the kind of surface are painted from what is known.

titan.basis: In visible light Titan's thick orange haze hides the ground completely (Voyager, Cassini, Huygens). Drawn as the haze: a slightly darker northern hemisphere and faint bands, no surface features.

proteus.basis: Voyager 2 (1989): dark, neutral grey (albedo about 0.1), heavily cratered, with the large crater Pharos. No global map exists.

nereid.basis: Voyager 2 saw Nereid only as a few pixels: neutral grey, albedo about 0.16. The pattern is a generic cratered surface.

charon.basis: New Horizons (2015): neutral grey water ice, albedo about 0.4, with a reddish-brown north polar cap (Mordor Macula) and a long canyon belt. Painted as a generic cratered grey surface until the New Horizons map is processed (#23).

styx.basis: Too small for New Horizons to map; its brightness implies clean water ice like its siblings. Generic cratered surface (#23).

nix.basis: New Horizons (2015): bright, water-ice covered, with one reddish crater. Generic cratered surface (#23).

kerberos.basis: New Horizons (2015): a bright double-lobed body, water ice. Generic cratered surface (#23).

hydra.basis: New Horizons (2015): the brightest of Pluto's small moons, almost pure water ice. Generic cratered surface (#23).

dysnomia.basis: Eris's moon is very dark, albedo about 0.05 (ALMA, Brown & Butler 2018/2023), unlike its bright planet. Generic cratered surface (#23).

namaka.basis: Haumea's moons show crystalline water ice in their spectra (Barkume et al. 2006); albedo assumed high like Haumea's. Generic cratered surface (#23).

hiiaka.basis: Hiʻiaka's spectrum is dominated by crystalline water ice (Barkume et al. 2006); albedo assumed high. Generic cratered surface (#23).

s20151364721.basis: Makemake's moon is as dark as charcoal, albedo about 0.04 (Parker et al. 2016), against a bright planet. Generic cratered surface (#23).

jupiter-inner.basis: Galileo and Voyager: dark and red (Amalthea is one of the reddest bodies known), dusted with sulphur from Io.

jupiter-prograde.basis: The Himalia group: dark, neutral grey, like carbon-rich (C-type) asteroids; Himalia was imaged by Cassini and New Horizons as a grey speck.

jupiter-retrograde.basis: The Ananke and Pasiphae groups: captured, dark (albedo about 0.05), grey to slightly red in ground-based colour measurements.

jupiter-carme.basis: The Carme group: dark and light red, and uniform in colour, pointing to one shattered parent body.

saturn-ringmoons.basis: Cassini: icy, cream-coloured and coated with ring particles; Pan and Atlas are smooth, with few craters.

saturn-coorbital.basis: Cassini: bright, icy and heavily cratered, with a slight cream tint.

saturn-alkyonides.basis: Cassini: Methone is as smooth as an egg, with no craters seen; these tiny moons sit in faint rings of dust.

saturn-trojans.basis: Cassini: among the brightest moons, coated with fine ice from Enceladus's plume, with soft, buried craters.

saturn-inuit.basis: The Inuit group: dark and light red in colour measurements; Cassini saw them only as points of light.

saturn-gallic.basis: The Gallic group: dark and light red, like the Inuit group.

saturn-norse.basis: The Norse group orbits backwards like Phoebe and is thought to share its dark, neutral grey material.

uranus-inner.basis: Voyager 2 and Hubble: dark (albedo below 0.1) and neutral grey, like Uranus's dark rings; Puck is cratered.

uranus-red.basis: Ground-based colour measurements: dark and clearly red.

uranus-irregular.basis: Captured moons seen only as points of light: assumed dark, grey to slightly red like the other irregular moons.

neptune-inner.basis: Voyager 2: dark (albedo about 0.09) and neutral to slightly red; Larissa is cratered.

neptune-irregular.basis: Captured moons seen only as points of light; Halimede is neutral grey. Assumed dark and grey.
